focused_use_paragraphs:
**(a) Curve families and motions.** A **curve family** of the model is a map
$x:J\to Q$, $x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})$, of class $C^{2}$ on $J$
([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]); its **coordinate velocities** are
$w_{i}:=x_{i}'$ on $J$, written $w=(w_{1},\dots,w_{N}):J\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$.
A curve family is a **motion** of the model when
$$m_{i}\ddot x_{i}(t)=F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N,\ t\in J),$$
the notion of clause (c) of [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]. Every quantity of
this definition is defined for an arbitrary curve family; the balance theorems
of this page state which of their properties use the equations of motion.
Along a curve family the force map is evaluated at $(t,x(t),w(t))\in
I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$; when the model invokes the
external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of [[post-cm02-interactions]],
the maps $F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $F_{ij}$ are evaluated at their declared
arguments on the motion's state graph, where the presentation is an identity
for $F_{i}$.

**(c) Angular momentum, torque, internal torque sum.** Let a **reference
curve** $o:J\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of class $C^{1}$ be given: a point about which
moments are taken, allowed to move (a constant map $o\equiv o_{0}$ is the
fixed-origin case). Define the **angular momentum about $o$** and the **total
torque about $o$** by
$$J_{o}(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times p_{i}(t),\qquad T_{o}(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),w(t)\bigr),$$
with dimensions $[J_{o}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (read in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\,\mathrm s^{-1}$) and
$[T_{o}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in $\mathrm N\,\mathrm m$). When the
model invokes the external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of
[[post-cm02-interactions]], define in addition the **external torque** and the
**internal torque sum**
$$T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}(t):=\sum_{i}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-o(t)\bigr)\times F_{i}^{\mathrm{ext}}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),w_{i}(t)\bigr),\qquad I(t):=\sum_{i<j}\bigl(x_{i}(t)-x_{j}(t)\bigr)\times F_{ij}\bigl(t,x_{i}(t),x_{j}(t),w_{i}(t),w_{j}(t)\bigr).$$
The sum $I$ does not involve $o$; it is defined whenever the pair
presentation is declared. The identity $T_{o}=T_{o}^{\mathrm{ext}}+I$ uses the
antisymmetry $F_{ji}=-F_{ij}$ of clause (ii)1 of that postulate to reindex the
ordered pairs and is proved as step 1.1 of the angular-momentum balance of
this page.

- **The internal torque sum is not a smallness statement.** $I$ collects one
  term per unordered pair of labels; its vanishing is a hypothesis on the
  evaluated pair forces (for instance the centrality clause (ii)2 of
  [[post-cm02-interactions]] implies it), not a consequence of the equations
  of motion.

focused_use_paragraphs:
**(a) Potential representation of the force map.** A model **presents its
force map through a potential** when it declares a function
$$U:I_{0}\times Q\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$
of class $C^{2}$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), of
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in joules), with
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$
for every $(t,x,v)$ of the state domain; here $\nabla_{x_{i}}U$ is the
gradient of $u\mapsto U(t,x_{1},\dots,x_{i-1},u,x_{i+1},\dots,x_{N})$ at
$u=x_{i}$. More generally, a model may declare **residual forces**
$d_{i}:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of the standing
regularity of clause (iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and present
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v);$$
the pair $(U,d)$ is then the model's presentation and
$F_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}:=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U$ is its **potential part**. The scalar
$U$ is a **potential energy** for the model's potential part; the framework's
earlier admission of potentials in [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (iii) is
the special case $d\equiv0$. A model that presents its whole force map this
way with $d\equiv0$ is a **global potential model** (the term "conservative
model" is used only in this sense).

**(g) Status.** The potential, its normalization, the residual forces and the
declaration of a potential presentation are model data; the closed/exact
statements of (d)-(f) are cited mathematics about the declared field. This
item asserts no conservation law, no force law of nature and no measured
value.

**(d) Potential presentation, residual forces and energy.** The model
**presents its force law through a potential** when it declares a function
$U:Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ ([[def-derivative]]) of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, read in joules, and a **residual force**
$d:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of the standing regularity of
(a), with
$$F(t,x,v)=-U'(x)+d(t,x,v)\qquad\bigl((t,x,v)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R\bigr);$$
here $U'$ is the ordinary derivative. This is the one-coordinate case of the
potential presentation of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause
(a) for a time- and velocity-independent potential, and the scalar
$U$ is a **potential energy** of the model's potential part. The model is a
**global potential model** (equivalently, in the framework's usage, a
**conservative model**) when $d\equiv0$; the term "conservative" is used only
in this sense, as recorded in that definition. For a conservative model the
**mechanical energy** is the function
$$E:Q\times\mathbb R\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad E(x,v):=\tfrac12 m v^{2}+U(x),$$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. For a model with declared residual
forces, the **mechanical energy along a motion** $x:J\to Q$ is
$E(t):=\tfrac12m\,x'(t)^{2}+U(x(t))$; it is defined along curve families even
though the force law is not presented through $U$ alone.

- **The declared representative of the potential.** As in
  [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c), adding a constant
  to $U$ changes no force; for the scalar class no time-dependent
  normalization is admitted in clause (d), because the potential is declared
  time-independent, and every energy statement of this page names the
  representative it uses.

Adopt the force model, one inertial frame, and the potential presentation of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (a): a $C^{2}$ potential
$$U:I_{0}\times Q\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d_{i}$ of the standing
regularity, with
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$
on the state domain. Let $x:J\to Q$ be a **motion** of the model on an
interval $J$ with nonempty interior, write $\mathfrak d_{i}(t):=d_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))$
for the evaluated residual forces and
$$E(t):=K(t)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)$$
for the mechanical energy of the definition (clause (b)). Then:

The representative $U$ is the one declared by the model; replacing $U$ by
$U+c(t)$ changes $E$ by $c(t)$ and $E'$ by $c'(t)$, as recorded in
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c). The statement is read
in the fixed frame; no empirical content is claimed.

[L1] Notation ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clauses (a)-(b), [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]): $K$, $W$ and $\mathcal P$ are the kinetic energy, work and power of the definition; $Q$ is nonempty and open; $U$ is $C^{2}$ hence $C^{1}$; $t\mapsto U(t,x(t))$ is defined on $J$; the equation of motion is $m_{i}\ddot x_{i}=F_{i}(t,x,w)$ with $F_{i}=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U+d_{i}$, so that $m_{i}\ddot x_{i}(t)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x(t))+\mathfrak d_{i}(t)$ with $\mathfrak d_{i}(t)=d_{i}(t,x(t),w(t))$.

- **Conservation is conditional and representation-dependent.** Clause 2 requires the representative $U$ to be time-independent and the residual forces to vanish; a potential $U+c(t)$ with time-dependent $c$ turns a conserved model into a presentation with $E'=c'(t)$, as clause (c) of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] records. Energy statements therefore name the representative.

Adopt the following gravitational model and empirical premises for the
two-body part of this page, inside the force and interaction branches of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]] and the

branch is a model of class (i) of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with
$J_0=(0,\infty)$, $Q=\{x=(x_1,x_2):x_1\ne x_2\}$, masses $m_1,m_2>0$ in the
equation of motion, and the **gravitational pair potential**
$$U(x_1,x_2)=-\frac{G_{\mathrm N}\,m_1^{g}m_2^{g}}{\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert},$$
where $G_{\mathrm N}>0$ is the **Newtonian constant of gravitation**, a
constant of dimension $\ell^{3}\mu^{-1}\tau^{-2}$ read in
$\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and $m_1^{g},m_2^{g}>0$ are the
**gravitational coupling parameters** of the labels, primitive model data
distinct from the inertial masses $m_1,m_2$ ([[post-cm02-interactions]]

class (i) is $u(\rho)=-\kappa/\rho$ with
$$\kappa:=G_{\mathrm N}\,m_1^{g}m_2^{g}>0,\qquad\text{dimension } \mu\ell^{3}\tau^{-2};$$
it is of class $C^\infty$ on $(0,\infty)$, the model has no external forces,
and coincident configurations are excluded. The force is attractive, and its
inverse-square form is an **adopted law** of this branch, not a consequence
of the equation of motion.

**(ii) The empirical mass identification.** For the quantitative
applications of this page, adopt in addition the identification
$$m_i^{g}=m_i\qquad(i=1,2)$$
of the gravitational coupling parameters with the inertial masses. This is an
**empirical assumption**, not part of clause (i) and not a consequence of the
equation of motion ([[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (vi)); it is the
content of the weak equivalence principle for these labels, and it is
adopted here only where a statement explicitly says so. When it is adopted,
$\kappa=G_{\mathrm N}m_1m_2$, and every conclusion that uses it inherits its
empirical status; statements that never invoke clause (ii) remain conditional
on clause (i) alone, with $\kappa$ expressed through $m_1^{g},m_2^{g}$.

focused_use_paragraphs: 4.1 For the converse, let a torque-free motion have constant body angular velocity $\omega\equiv\omega_{0}$. By [L6] its body angular velocity satisfies $I\omega'+\omega\times I\omega=0$; with $\omega'=0$ this reads $\omega_{0}\times I\omega_{0}=0$, so $I\omega_{0}$ is a real multiple of $\omega_{0}$ by alternation [L5]: if $\omega_{0}\neq0$ there is $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with $I\omega_{0}=\lambda\omega_{0}$, so $\omega_{0}$ is an eigenvector of $I$. Within its eigenspace choose the unit vector $e_j=\omega_0/\|\omega_0\|_2$. Starting with the original principal vectors in that eigenspace, subtract their projection onto $e_j$, and normalize a nonzero remainder if the eigenspace has dimension greater than one; subtract the projections onto both selected vectors and normalize a nonzero remainder if its dimension is three. Such remainders exist because the original vectors span the eigenspace; linear combinations remain eigenvectors for the same eigenvalue, and the projection subtractions give orthonormality by [L5]. Retain the original orthonormal vectors in the other eigenspaces. This supplies an adapted orthonormal principal basis directly in dimension three. Negating one of the other two basis vectors if necessary makes it positively oriented. In this adapted basis $\omega_0=\Omega e_j$, $\Omega=\|\omega_0\|_2\ne0$, without a simple-spectrum hypothesis; if $\omega_{0}=0$, then $R'=R[0]=0$ and $R$ is constant by [L4]. In the nonzero case the path satisfies the identity of clause 1 with rate $\Omega$, so clauses 2 and 3 apply to it. This is clause 4. [step 2.1, given, L5, L6, algebra] ∎

focused_use_paragraphs:
- **Symmetries are properties of the model, not of the kinematics.** The
  symmetry criteria of this page are identities imposed on the model's
  declared mechanical Lagrangian $L=K-U$ and its residual forces
  ([[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]); the affine structure
  of the spacetime, the availability of every inertial frame and the Galilean
  transformation law of the description are kinematic facts of the framework
  and do not by themselves make any potential invariant. Concretely, for the
  uniform-force model of the framework with potential
  $U=-\sum_{i}m_{i}\,\mathbf g\cdot x_{i}$ one has
  $\sum_{i}\nabla_{x_{i}}U=-M_{\mathrm{tot}}\mathbf g$, so the translation
  condition of [[pthm-cm08-translation]] holds exactly for directions
  $a\perp\mathbf g$; for every such model the momentum component along a
  direction with $a\cdot\mathbf g\ne0$ is not conserved, and the sharpness
  clauses of [[pthm-cm08-translation]] and [[pthm-cm08-boost-boundary]] locate
  the failure at the maximal motion through any state with $a\cdot\nabla U\ne0$.
  Likewise a confining external potential such as
  $U=\tfrac{k}{2}\sum_{i}\lvert x_{i}-x_{i}^{0}\rvert^{2}$ fails the
  translation condition at every configuration whose centre of mass differs
  from the reference configuration, and both the momentum and the boost charge
  of [[pthm-cm08-boost-boundary]] are then unavailable.

- **Rotation is not translation.** The rotation condition of
  [[pthm-cm08-rotation]] is compatible with a confining central potential: for
  $U$ depending only on the labels through rotation-invariant combinations the
  angular-momentum charge may be conserved even when the translation charges
  are not. The conservation statements are therefore separate conditional
  claims, one per symmetry datum, and no global "conservation of everything"
  is available: a model can possess one charge and fail another.

$$\dot I=0,\qquad \dot\theta=\frac{\partial h}{\partial I}(I),\qquad\theta(t)=\theta(0)+t\,\frac{\partial h}{\partial I}\bigl(I(0)\bigr)\pmod{\mathbb Z^{n}},$$

   frequency vector;
5. **(radian rescaling)** with the rescaled coordinates
   $\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}:=2\pi\theta$ and
   $I^{\mathrm{rad}}:=I/(2\pi)$ one has
   $\omega=\sum_{i}d\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}_{i}\wedge dI^{\mathrm{rad}}_{i}$,

   $H=\tilde h(I^{\mathrm{rad}})$ with

   $\dot\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}=\partial\tilde h/\partial I^{\mathrm{rad}}$;
   the components $\partial h/\partial I_{i}$ are **cyclic frequencies**
   (cycles per unit time), not angular rates, the angular rates being
   $2\pi\,\partial h/\partial I_{i}$.

1. **(complete integral)** $S$ is of class $C^{\infty}$ on $V$ and solves
   the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation
   $S_{t}+H(x,S_{x})=0$ on $V$; the mixed derivative is
   $S_{x\alpha}=-m\omega\,\csc(\omega t)$, so $S$ is a complete integral of
   the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation at every point of $V$
   ([[def-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-equation]],
   [[def-cm14-complete-integral]]).
2. **(characteristics)** for every $(t_{0},x_{0},\alpha_{0})\in V$ and
   every real $\beta$, the curve
   $$x(t)=\alpha_{0}\cos(\omega t)-\frac{\beta}{m\omega}\sin(\omega t)$$
   satisfies $S_{\alpha}(t,x(t),\alpha_{0})=\beta$, and with
   $p(t):=S_{x}(t,x(t),\alpha_{0})$ the pair $(x,p)$ solves
   $x'=H_{p}$, $p'=-H_{x}$ on every interval on which
   $\sin(\omega t)\neq0$; hence $x$ is a motion of the harmonic model with
   $p=mx'$ and $S_{\alpha}$ is constant along it
   ([[pthm-cm14-hamilton-jacobi-characteristics]]).
3. **(action-angle chart)** the map
$$(\theta,I)\longmapsto(x,p)=\Bigl(\sqrt{\frac{I}{\pi m\omega}}\,\sin(2\pi\theta),\ \sqrt{\frac{Im\omega}{\pi}}\,\cos(2\pi\theta)\Bigr)$$is a $C^{\infty}$ chart of the region $I>0$ with $\{x,p\}=1$ for the
   presentation's bracket, i.e. a canonical chart of
   [[def-cm13-canonical-form]] with
   $\omega_{\mathrm{form}}=d\theta\wedge dI$ in the period-one convention
   of [[def-action-and-angle-coordinates]], and in it
   $$H=h(I)=\frac{I}{T},$$
   so that every motion satisfies $\dot I=0$,
   $\dot\theta=1/T$ ([[pthm-cm14-action-angle]] clause 4).
4. **(action normalization)** the action coordinate is the period integral
   $$I=\oint p\,dx=\int_{0}^{T}p(t)\,x'(t)\,dt$$
   along one period of the oscillator motion, in the period-one
   normalization discussed in the remark of [[pthm-cm14-action-angle]].
5. **(radian convention)** with $\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}:=2\pi\theta$ and
   $I^{\mathrm{rad}}:=I/(2\pi)$ the chart becomes
   $x=\sqrt{2I^{\mathrm{rad}}/(m\omega)}\,\sin\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}$,
   $p=\sqrt{2I^{\mathrm{rad}}m\omega}\,\cos\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}$ with
   $H=\omega I^{\mathrm{rad}}$ and
   $\dot\theta^{\mathrm{rad}}=\omega$, which is the radian chart of the
   sources ([[cor-cm-action-angle-radian-scaling]]).
